rows.claim: People expect passing taxRate 0 to quoteOrder to charge no tax, but the code really treats 0 as missing via rate || 0.2 and applies 20% tax instead.
People expect passing taxRate 0 to quoteOrder to mean no tax is charged, but the code really treats 0 as missing via rate || 0.2 and adds 20 percent tax instead.
People expect run_import to import the same records again on a second call, but the code really reuses dedupe's mutable default seen set across calls so the second call writes nothing and returns 0.

People expect run_import to write the same records again on a second call with the same input, but the code really reuses dedupe's mutable default seen set across calls so the second call writes nothing and returns 0.

People expect fetchAllOrders to return every order by following nextCursor until it is null, but the code really stops silently after 5 pages by default and returns only those ids with no error or indication that more pages remain.

People expect fetchAllOrders to return every order by following nextCursor until it is null, but the code really stops silently after the default maxPages of 5 pages and returns only those ids with no error or indication of truncation.

People expect the median latency of four successful routes taking 10, 20, 30, and 40 ms to be 25 ms as the average of the two middle values, but the code really returns 30 ms because it picks the single element at index floor(length/2) without averaging.

People expect report with successful route latencies 10, 20, 30 and 40 ms to return a median of 25 ms as the average of the two middle values, but the code really returns 30 ms because median picks the upper middle element instead of averaging it with 20 ms.

People expect withRetry to throw the original 429 error immediately after the third and final failed attempt, but the code really sleeps for another 400ms backoff after that last failure and then throws a generic 'gave up' error that discards the original error.

People expect withRetry to surface the original 429 error after the third failed attempt without an extra pointless wait, but the code really sleeps for another 400 ms after that final failure and then throws a generic 'gave up' error that discards the original error.
